knowledge_gaps: The residual is bounded by one logit unit, while SASRec scores have an unspecified scale. Report support coverage, positive/negative support distributions, learned gate values, and score differences near rank 10; otherwise a null result could reflect insufficient influence.

SASRec plus shuffled-text scoring cannot isolate the benefit of requiring two witnesses. Include a matched one-witness lexical scorer and, if budget permits, the starting pooling residual. An unstratified text permutation can confound semantic alignment with text availability, document length and item frequency.

Candidate-conditioned scoring changes computational cost substantially. An O(L) scan per candidate-prefix query can require O(BL²) scan work for position-specific training targets, plus sparse similarity computation. Full-catalog inference needs an explicit chunking and memory plan; one added parameter does not justify code difficulty 4.

Feature-only causal checks can miss future leakage in candidate-specific scoring. Compare complete scores for fixed candidates before and after future masking, and require the structured feature carrier to enforce each scored position's prefix boundary.

Reproduction remains incomplete: exact baseline settings, remaining GPU budget, trial allocations, checkpoint cadence, shuffle scope and seed, and the structured scoring interface are unspecified. The optimized scan also needs explicit insertion, decay and running-best update equations.

Distinct witnesses can support different candidate attributes without establishing one recurring interest. Duplicate descriptions and brand boilerplate can also satisfy corroboration. Measure these shortcuts and support availability by history length before interpreting gains.

No host validation results establish improvement. Originality 4 and potential 7 remain provisional; related work should cover item-to-item and content-based history aggregation directly, rather than relying mainly on recency and perturbation references.
